newsitem.title: FRANCE: Snecma sees return towards breakeven.
newsitem.headline: Snecma sees return towards breakeven.

text.p: French state-owned aero-engine maker Snecma expects to return towards break-even this year, the company's new chairman said in remarks published on Friday.

"The parent company, which accounts for half the group's turnover, should be even more strongly in deficit this year. The group itself should be approaching balance," Jean-Paul Bechat said in an interview with Les Echos financial daily.
Sources close to the company had told in Reuters in April it was expecting to halve its losses in 1996, and again in 1997, from a 1.244 billion franc deficit in 1995.
Bechat was appointed to run the company in June following the ouster of his predecessor, Bernard Dufour.

Bechat told Les Echos he expected significant improvement in Snecma's finances in 1997 due to lower costs and a "lively" pick-up in orders. Engine deliveries would double in both 1996 and 1997, he said.
